title: Analog quantum simulation of Shastry-Sutherland Ising materials
authors: Vahagn Mkhitaryan, Milan Kornjača, Mao Lin, Alexander Schuckert, Majd Hamdan, Sergio H. Cantú, Ammar Ali, Tommaso Macrí, Nathan Gemelke, Alexander Keesling, Peter Komar, Travis S. Humble, Alexei Bylinski, Pedro L. S. Lopes, Fangli Liu, Alexandra Boltasseva, Mikhail D. Lukin, Arnab Banerjee, Vladimir M. Shalaev, Sheng-Tao Wang
abstract: Frustrated magnets host rich emergent behavior because competing interactions generate dense manifolds of low-energy states. The Ising Shastry-Sutherland model is a paradigmatic setting, motivated experimentally by Ising-like rare-earth tetraborides such as TmB$_4$ and ErB$_4$, whose field-induced magnetization plateaus have motivated extensive microscopic modeling. Yet how tunable quantum fluctuations reorganize this material-motivated phase diagram remains largely unexplored. Here, we realize a transverse- and longitudinal-field Ising model on the Shastry-Sutherland lattice using a programmable Rydberg-atom array. We map its quantum phase diagram using density matrix renormalization group calculations and probe corresponding signatures experimentally in arrays containing more than 110 atoms. Beyond the established classical phases, the calculations identify two regimes absent in the classical limit and stabilized at finite transverse field: a $2/5$ filling plateau whose finite stability region emerges from a classically degenerate phase boundary and a symmetry-preserving quantum-dimer regime replacing classically selected collinear order. Experiments on finite open arrays reveal signatures consistent with these regimes across three boundary-pinning conditions, with the resulting response maps agreeing qualitatively with the calculated phase diagram. Our results establish programmable Rydberg-atom arrays as tools for exploring frustrated, material-motivated Hamiltonians and motivate searches for new, quantum-driven magnetization plateaus and quantum-dimer behavior in ErB$_4$ under a transverse field or in strain-tuned TmB$_4$.
summary: This paper uses programmable Rydberg-atom arrays to simulate the quantum phase diagram of Ising magnets on the Shastry-Sutherland lattice, motivated by rare-earth materials. By combining DMRG calculations with experiments, the authors identify and confirm the existence of quantum-fluctuation-stabilized phases, such as 2/5 filling plateaus and quantum-dimer states. This establishes Rydberg arrays as a powerful tool for exploring frustrated quantum matter.
main_problem: The study investigates how tunable quantum fluctuations reorganize the classically frustrated phase diagram of Ising-like magnets, motivated by rare-earth tetraborides.
main_result: The work experimentally and theoretically identifies novel quantum-stabilized phases, including a 2/5 filling plateau and a symmetry-preserving quantum-dimer regime, beyond the classical predictions.
method: The research combines Density Matrix Renormalization Group (DMRG) calculations to map the phase diagram with experiments using programmable Rydberg-atom arrays to probe these quantum signatures.
model_or_system: The system is an Ising magnet on the Shastry-Sutherland lattice, modeled by an effective Hamiltonian realized using Rydberg atoms in optical-tweezer arrays. The platform allows independent control over geometry and external fields (transverse and longitudinal).
key_observables: Order parameters such as structure factors (for 1/3, 2/5, Néel phases), local dimer occupation ($\langle D_i^2 angle$), and dimer-dimer correlators ($C_{ij}$).
important_parameters: Transverse field strength (controlled by Rabi frequency $\Omega$) and detuning ($\Delta$), which tune the system between classical and quantum regimes.
main_assumptions: The primary assumption is that the Rydberg array can accurately simulate the complex, material-motivated Hamiltonian, and that the measured response maps reflect the underlying quantum phase diagram.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the crystal structure and mapping to the spin model, the calculated phase diagram showing classical and quantum regimes, and experimental response maps comparing different boundary pinning conditions for various order parameters.
paper_structure: The paper first establishes the physical motivation from rare-earth magnets, then details the mapping onto the Rydberg platform and the theoretical tools (DMRG). It proceeds to calculate and identify quantum regimes (2/5 plateau, quantum dimer) and concludes by presenting experimental measurements confirming these predicted signatures across varying boundary conditions.
why_interesting: This work is highly relevant as it uses Rydberg arrays—a premier tool in AMO physics—to simulate complex, frustrated quantum Hamiltonians, directly bridging fundamental condensed matter theory with cutting-edge quantum simulation hardware.
